items.title: Insurance analysts pressured to play down climate risks to cut prices
items.summary: Insurance industry professionals report that risk modellers are frequently pressured to manipulate climate risk assessments to justify lower policy prices. This practice raises concerns about the accuracy of risk modeling within the sector.

brief.what: Five industry professionals have disclosed that it is common practice for risk modellers to be pressured into altering their analyses to artificially reduce insurance prices. This suggests a systemic effort to downplay climate-related risks to maintain competitive pricing.
brief.who: The main actors are unnamed industry professionals who provided information to the Financial Times regarding internal practices at insurance firms.
brief.context: Insurance companies rely on complex risk models to determine premiums, particularly regarding environmental threats. These models are intended to reflect the actual financial exposure posed by climate change.
brief.why: According to the professionals, the pressure is applied to artificially lower prices, implying a conflict between accurate risk assessment and commercial pricing strategies.

items.title: Milestone cancer vaccine success leaves hard questions unanswered
items.author: Jocelyn Kaiser
items.summary: A joint mRNA vaccine developed by Merck and Moderna has demonstrated success in reducing the risk of melanoma recurrence. Researchers are now investigating the underlying biological mechanisms behind this efficacy.

brief.what: An mRNA vaccine developed by Merck and Moderna has successfully reduced the risk of melanoma returning in patients. While the clinical results are positive, the specific reasons for the vaccine's effectiveness remain unclear.
brief.who: Merck and Moderna are the pharmaceutical companies responsible for developing the mRNA vaccine.
brief.context: The vaccine is designed to treat melanoma, a serious form of skin cancer, by preventing its return after initial treatment.
brief.why: The article notes that while the vaccine slashes the risk of melanoma's return, the precise biological explanation for why this occurs is not yet understood.
brief.next: Researchers are working to answer the remaining questions regarding the vaccine's mechanism of action.
